So — first pass below. Kept language tight per Amanda's ask; this can be copy/pasted into the exhibit section of the Order Form. Thoughts, Laura?

Proposed exhibit snippets (redline-friendly):

1) SOC 2 Artifact Access
"Customer may request on-site or remote access to SOC 2 artifacts for the definitions covered by the Agreement. Redwood will provide two (2) access windows per contract year, each window not to exceed forty-eight (48) consecutive hours. Requests for access must be submitted at least ten (10) business days in advance. Redwood will provide exported artifact packages and a read-only review session with a Redwood engineer during the window. Access does not include keys or other artifacts that would expose other customers' data, and access to production systems is subject to Redwood's operational policies and gating."

2) Penetration Test Coordination
"Customer may conduct a penetration test against Redwood-managed staging infrastructure with at least ten (10) business days' prior written notice. Tests must be scoped to Customer-specific tenant resources and may not access shared control plane or infrastructure components. Redwood will provide a staging environment baseline and a temporary token provisioning process. Any findings that require production changes will be handled via Redwood's standard vulnerability remediation process. Testing that would require elevated access or impact to other customers will not be permitted without express written agreement and may require a separate commercial arrangement."

3) Carveouts (short)
"Redwood will not disclose credentials, ephemeral keys, or other customer secrets for cross-tenant systems in any evidence package. Where necessary, Redwood will provide sanitized, scoped artifacts or summary attestations in lieu of raw secrets."

Ben — good concise draft. A few Legal notes to make this redline-safe:

- For SOC2 artifacts, replace 'on-site or remote access' with 'delivery of exported artifacts and a scheduled review session' to avoid custody claims.
- Add a clause that Redwood may redact or withhold any information required by law or that would materially increase risk to third parties.
- For the pen-test paragraph, we should explicitly limit liability and require that the Customer carry cyber insurance covering testing activities; propose a sentence linking acceptable testing approaches to Redwood's "Testing Guidelines" hosted at a URL (we can use a placeholder).
- Add a final sentence to the exhibit that calls out escalation path: if an attempted test is likely to affect non-customer resources, Redwood will pause testing and schedule a remediation/retest window.

I'll prepare a redline PDF that substitutes 'access' language for 'delivery + review' and attaches a 1-page evidence matrix we can share. Will aim to send by end of day tomorrow (12/03).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
